DONE.text: N=10 cost experiment: 50 queries, four routing arms (A0 global, A1 transactive, A2 static, A3 similarity), gpt-4o-mini, 10 seeds, frozen tau
Reported effect-size estimator is Kerby (2014) matched-pairs rank-biserial r = (T+ - T-)/(T+ + T-) over the n_eff non-zero pairs; zero_method=wilcox retained; Rosenthal z/sqrt(N) retired
Routing threshold tau frozen for the N=10 run is 0.351493 (same asmos_tau in both E2 new-topic configs)

ASMOS ownership layer: ownership is learned online from verification-gated reputation; a verified claim raises an agent's topic ownership, a refuted claim lowers it; queries route to the learned owner with a confidence-gated fallback to global search; router scores Sim x Ownership with a tau-gated fallback

DATA.text: The transactive evaluation set has 50 queries in five query classes Q1-Q5; global search consults a candidate set of 32.0 on average

FOUND.text: On the constructed 50-query transactive corpus (gpt-4o-mini, 10 seeds), transactive routing (A1) used 22.1% fewer LLM total tokens per query than global search (A0), a mean of 39.8 fewer tokens per query, with a bootstrap 95% CI over queries of 17.9% to 26.3% and per-seed reductions between 21.9% and 22.2%.

A one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the 50 per-query token differences between A0 and A1 gave W = 1141.5 and p = 6.788e-09 (48 non-zero pairs of 50); the matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation is r = 0.941 (T+ = 1141.5, T- = 34.5, z = 5.679).

The width of the bootstrap interval (8.3 percentage points) is set by heterogeneity between queries, not by seed noise: the per-seed standard deviation of the reduction is 0.07 percentage points, so additional seeds would not narrow the interval.

Across 50 queries and 10 seeds the mean LLM tokens per query were 180.2 for A0, 140.4 for A1, 179.3 for A2 (ownership frozen at the prior) and 123.4 for A3 (similarity routing without ownership); A2 is within 0.9 tokens of A0 and 38.9 tokens above A1.
In the five newest seeds (66, 77, 88, 99, 110), answerability was 0.98 for A0, A1 and A2 and 0.58 for the similarity-based arm A3 in every seed.

In the five newest seeds (66, 77, 88, 99, 110), answer accuracy was 0.72 for A0 and A2 in every seed, between 0.68 and 0.70 for A1 (below A0 in every seed) and between 0.54 and 0.56 for A3; no paired test of the accuracy difference is available and the grading procedure is not documented.
In the five newest seeds (66, 77, 88, 99, 110), route@1 was 0.909 for A1, 0.0 for A0 and A2 (which do not route to a single owner) and 0.614 for A3.

In the new-topic regime with the all-mpnet-base-v2 embedder (5 seeds, 10 steps, 5 evaluation queries per step), ASMOS reached a cumulative regret of 3.24 (std 1.30) with 0 retrains and routed the new topic in 5 of 5 seeds; a frozen classifier never routed it (regret 10.0), a classifier retrained every 5 steps had regret 4.8 (std 0.4, 2 retrains) and one retrained every 10 steps had regret 9.0 (1 retrain); the artifact also records 10 labels consumed by ASMOS, as by the retraining classifiers; the definition of that counter is not documented.

In the new-topic regime with the bge-m3 embedder (5 seeds, 10 steps), ASMOS reached a cumulative regret of 0.92 (std 0.41) with 0 retrains and routed the new topic in 5 of 5 seeds; the classifier baselines were identical to the all-mpnet-base-v2 run (10.0, 4.8 and 9.0).
In both new-topic runs, per-step answerability is identical for all four arms (0.0 at step 0 rising to 1.0 at step 10), so it does not separate ASMOS from the classifiers in that regime.

In a single stationary-regime run with no seeds and no stated query count (the recorded values are multiples of 1/11), ASMOS with the MiniLM-L6-v2 embedder and the classifier both had route@1 1.0, and the recorded answerability was 0.909 for ASMOS against 0.727 for the classifier, with no test; with the lexical-hash fallback embedder ASMOS route@1 was 0.667 against 1.0 for the classifier, so ASMOS was not routing-competitive there.

On 24 question-answering items from the RULER benchmark (gpt-4o-mini, single run), exact-match scores were 0.3333 for No-Memory, 0.7083 for RAG, 0.1667 for ASMOS-memory and 0.625 for ASMOS+RAG (equal to the containment scores in every row), with token-F1 of 0.5642, 0.7513, 0.4155 and 0.4329.

Paired token-F1 differences on the 24 questions: RAG exceeds ASMOS-memory by 0.3358 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.1494 to 0.5228); ASMOS+RAG is below RAG by 0.3184 (CI -0.4990 to -0.1406); ASMOS+RAG minus ASMOS-memory is +0.0174 (CI -0.1546 to +0.1862, which spans zero).

On this static single-agent span-retrieval question-answering task ASMOS-memory alone scored below No-Memory and below RAG, and ASMOS did not beat RAG; the authors state that ASMOS is not a question-answering-accuracy method.

In both new-topic runs (all-mpnet-base-v2 and bge-m3 embedders, 5 seeds each), ASMOS adapted to the new topic with zero retraining (0 retrain events in every seed); the artifacts record labels_consumed = 10 for ASMOS, the same as each retrained classifier, so zero added labels is not claimed.

The effect size reported is the matched-pairs rank-biserial correlation, chosen by the authors because it is the direct companion of the signed-rank test that was run and has a single definition; Rosenthal's z/sqrt(N) is not reported because its N can be read three ways (giving 0.803, 0.819 or 0.568 on the headline).
The signed-rank test keeps the zero_method wilcox (zero differences dropped) because switching to the Pratt method would change an already pre-registered p-value.
The number of non-zero pairs (n_eff) is reported beside every effect size because a bare r = 1.0 invites the false reading that every query improved.
No multiplicity correction is applied because the analysis is a single comparison (A0 versus A1).

The MiniLM embedder is the one used for the routing results reported in the project's documentation, because the authors regard the lexical-hash fallback as a degraded offline mode and not the evaluation baseline.

The effect size originally stored for the headline test (r = 0.688, labelled a rank-biserial correlation) and its z (4.865) were computed incorrectly and are superseded by r = 0.941 and z = 5.679; W, the one-sided p, the percentage reduction, the confidence interval and the per-seed spread did not change.

ASMOS (Adaptive Semantic Memory Operating System) is a shared semantic-memory layer for teams of LLM agents plus an ownership layer that decides which agent to ask: ownership of a topic is learned online from verification-gated reputation (a verified claim raises an agent's ownership of a topic, a refuted claim lowers it), and a query is routed to the learned owner, the router scoring similarity times ownership with a threshold-gated (tau) fallback to global search.

On the constructed asymmetric two-agent corpus, mean context tokens per query were 123.2 (A0), 83.6 (A1), 122.3 (A2) and 65.9 (A3), and the mean candidate-set size was 32.0, 20.8, 31.7 and 17.9 for the same four arms; the evaluation set has five query classes.

On the same corpus the mean within-domain cosine similarity of topic centroids was 0.2666, the mean cross-domain similarity 0.1024 and the maximum cross-domain similarity 0.2072, and the project's separability check returned go.
With 5 seeds the headline reduction recorded in the same result file was 22.109%; extending to 10 seeds shifted it by -0.0179 percentage points to 22.0911%.

Corrected signed-rank statistics are recorded for three other cost runs with 50 query pairs: gpt-4o-mini with 5 seeds (W = 1142.5, 48 non-zero pairs of 50, r = 0.943, p = 6.418e-09), qwen3-30b-a3b with 5 seeds (W = 1052.0, 46 of 50, r = 0.946, p = 1.145e-08) and a one-seed pilot with qwen-2.5-72b (W = 666.0, 36 of 50 with 14 zero differences, r = 1.0, p = 8.259e-08); their percentage reductions are not recorded in the package.
In the same four-system run, mean total tokens per question were 152.0 for No-Memory, 711.4 for RAG, 353.7 for ASMOS-memory and 1181.9 for ASMOS+RAG.

The memory contract (version 1.2) fixes a checkpoint schema whose fields have system, LLM or computed origin, a lifecycle from NEW through VALIDATED, PROMOTED and MERGED to ARCHIVED and FORGOTTEN, and invariants that include never forgetting the immutable layer.

The 10-seed cost result file does not record which embedder was used; the two new-topic runs record all-mpnet-base-v2 and bge-m3; the single stationary run records MiniLM-L6-v2 and a lexical-hash fallback; the classifier baselines give identical new-topic results under both embedders, and their input features are not recorded.

With ownership frozen at its prior (A2) the router never routes to a single owner (route@1 0.0), falls back to global search and recovers almost none of the saving; because A2 collapses to global search, the ablation contrasts routing with no routing. It is consistent with the saving requiring ownership that has moved above the routing threshold, but it cannot separate ownership evolution from, for example, a correctly set static ownership. (this is interpretation, not an established result)

LIMITS.text: The authors state that more seeds cannot narrow a confidence interval that is set by heterogeneity between queries.

The authors note that retrieval precision and recall, and route@1 and ownership accuracy, cannot be computed on the single-agent question-answering data because it has no relevant-document labels and no owner labels, and that the fusion system exercises routing with a single expert.
The authors state that ASMOS does not beat RAG on span-retrieval question answering and is not a question-answering-accuracy method.
The authors state that ownership asymmetry does not emerge organically because the corpus is deliberately constructed.

The authors list among their own caveats a convergence and sample-efficiency hypothesis that was tested; its result is not reported here because the result file is not in the package and its reporting is undecided.

The authors list three items as explicitly descoped: agent-specific memory projection (the store is global), contradiction detection (refutation is claimed only when supplied as a verification outcome) and continuous forgetting (present but off by default and not wired into a continuous loop).

The authors state that the routing threshold tau is tuned in-corpus rather than on a held-out split, that grading in the question-answering ladder is done by an LLM, that the deterministic ownership verification is not LLM-judged, that a memory-reuse threshold is an untuned placeholder that feeds none of the reported numbers, and that their multi-agent validation is one seedless run with an imposed partition; that run's result file is not in the package and no result from it is reported (checkpoint Q-003).
The authors state that the embedder of their earliest centerpiece run is unconfirmed, and that the LLM-token counts are exact API usage figures that do not depend on the embedder.

The authors exclude one embedder cell (bge-small in the new-topic replication) because the run fell back to the hash embedder and produced a degenerate regret, reporting it as incomplete rather than fabricated.
The authors note that a recorded continuous-integration pass or coverage artifact is an outstanding item.
Seeds 11 to 55 are pooled from a result file that is absent from the package, and per-seed accuracy, answerability, route@1 and context tokens exist only for seeds 66 to 110.
The grading procedure for answer accuracy on the transactive corpus is not stated and no paired test of accuracy exists, while A1 is below A0 in every one of five seeds.
No significance test, per-seed gap or interval exists for the A1 versus A2 comparison on the 50-query corpus; only pooled arm means are stored.
The corpus, query set, agent partition and code are not in the package, and the tuning of the classifier baselines (a classifier threshold of 0.5 against 0.351493 for ASMOS) is not documented.
The new-topic regime has 5 seeds and 5 evaluation queries per step, answerability is identical for all arms there, and ASMOS regret differs about threefold between the two embedders.
The four-system comparison is one run of 24 questions; exact match equals containment in every row, one system has token-F1 below its exact match, and no p-values are recorded.
The cross-embedder stationary run is a single run with no seeds and no stated query count.
For the other answering models only signed-rank statistics are recorded, one of them from a one-seed pilot; their percentage reductions are not in the package.
Several results listed in the project's README are not reported in this paper because their source result files are not in the package.
The headline saving is measured with a single answering model (gpt-4o-mini).
The token measure is the LLM usage recorded per query; the result file reports no separate cost for computing embeddings, updating ownership or producing verification outcomes.

No classifier updated online from the same labels is included; ASMOS and the retrained classifiers each consumed 10 labels, and ASMOS used the corpus-tuned threshold 0.351493 while the classifiers used 0.5.

The per-seed results agree closely (per-seed token reduction std 0.07 percentage points), so the recorded seeds are not independent replications, and the accuracy difference is 1 to 2 of 50 questions per seed.
The cost corpus has two agents, and the new-topic runs do not record how many agents take part.
Route@1 is recorded as a proportion without its denominator, and the criterion for a seed having routed the new topic is not recorded.

The pre-registration the authors cite for keeping zero differences dropped is not documented by a registry entry, date or protocol in the package (their correction record calls the stamped result files the pre-registration record), and the signed-rank tests of the other cost runs are reported without multiplicity correction.
